function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

message.content:
I don’t have a way to directly measure your current internet speed from here. The easiest way to check it yourself is to use an online speed test:

1. **Speedtest by Ookla** – Visit [speedtest.net](https://www.speedtest.net/) and click “Go.”  
2. **Fast.com** – Go to [fast.com](https://fast.com/) and it will automatically start measuring your download speed.  
3. **Google “internet speed test”** – Google’s built‑in test will pop up at the top of the search results; just click “Run Speed Test.”

These tests will give you your download speed, upload speed, and ping (latency). If you’re troubleshooting a specific issue (e.g., streaming buffering, lag in gaming, etc.), let me know and I can help interpret the results or suggest next steps!
